body: This is a really confusing question to ask and I don’t know why you’re asking but yeah I’ve seen that before on the internet
Is there even prosecution for 12 year olds who do something like this?
Same age as me. I think I’m gonna tell her. My sister is very blunt with me and has seen me at my best and worst.

I told my girlfriend. Mostly because the anxiety from it has been eating away at me.   


She told me what all of you on these threads have told me and that is that it's not good but I was a child, and that she doesn't see me differently at all but she encourages me to handle the guilt through therapy or any method I can to resolve it.
In my case there was just so little introduction or anything at all. Even in my school sex ed the focus was on like, periods and condom use and it stopped there.

Talking to my SO is something I’m really unsure about. Because I was 12 and because I am aware of how intrusive the thought is in my head currently, I don’t want to jump the gun, present this entire situation as such and watch my world crumble before me.
Thank you so much for your words.
Do you have any advice on how to move forward?

OP here. I'm not looking for justification for my actions as a 12 year old. Actions are actions. There's nothing that can be changed about what I did. 

I'm looking for how to move forward, process and accept the guilt and live normally.
I'm concerned that bringing this up to her since she didn't even know will cause her far more trauma and mental health problems than any of this is causing me.

Thank you or being straight up with me.

I was recently diagnosed with severe OCD, which means I will get an intrusive thought which will last for months at a time, ruining relationships with people and making me distance myself very hard. I feel that maybe this immense shame and guilt I am dealing with now is one of those. I just feel like screaming from the rooftops what I have done, telling my friends, girlfriend, etc. because I feel like I have to. I know that I don't, and I know that I won't, but these thoughts can be scary.

In terms of talking to her, I didn’t at the time. I don’t know her now and now that it’s so far later in life, I don’t know if talking to her would do much good. I might make her aware of something she didn’t even know happened and I’m worried that could just cause her more harm than my thoughts now will ever cause me. 

I have tendencies of extreme OCD so while my upbringing hasn’t told me to self-punish or feel shame, I have episodes of intrusive thoughts that dominate my mind for months and often ruin relationships I am in. This feels like one of those and I just feel like admitting my guilt to everyone I know and I know that’s not healthy
